doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Age at Sylvan Beach and his father's support during Prohibition
summary: He was sixteen or seventeen; his father supported him as long as he stayed sober, in Prohibition days.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So do you remember how old you were when you had this first experience in Sylvan Beach with this band?
I would say seventeen — sixteen, seventeen. I must have been seventeen otherwise my mother wouldn’t have allowed me to be in Sylvan Beach I guess you know.
So you came home and said: guess what I did, I played with this band.
Well how did they feel about that?

Well my father loved music and he was for me a hundred percent or whatever. Long as I didn’t drink or get smashed or anything. At that time anyway, there wasn’t any booze around, like it was all hidden, you know, what’d they say —
